chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
title: Monk and Bud Powell in New York; Jimmy Dorsey closes the club to hear Charlie Parker
summary: Monk befriends him, and at an after-hours jam Jimmy Dorsey has the doors shut to hear Charlie Parker and offers him a union card.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But the reason I'm saying this is that little incidents come to mind that happened. By this time, I had heard Bud Powell in New York, and had learned to respect him very much.

In New York I had heard him play quite a bit, and the pianist... Another one of the pianists that greeted me, who immediately made friends with me when I first went to New York was Thelonious Monk. He used to go out of his way to take me different places where things were happening, and listen to different musicians. And Bud was also a good friend of Monk's.

One night we were in the Yacht Club. I think it had changed to the Downbeat then. And there was a jam session going on after hours. Because Charlie Parker was there... And Jimmy Dorsey had never heard of Charlie Parker. Jimmy Dorsey came in, and it must have been just before the club was closing, because Jimmy Dorsey, I don't know, he gave the club owner some money and told him to close the doors and give everybody a drink -- and most of the people in there were musicians. He said, "I want to hear this man; he's going to give me a concert." And everybody was telling Charlie, "Jimmy Dorsey's in the house, and he wants to hear you" and all that. That was a big thing, you know, because Jimmy Dorsey was one of the big bandleaders of the day. At that particular time, he was playing at the Capitol Theatre.
So they closed the doors, and the session started. Jimmy Dorsey was just bowled over by Charlie Parker's playing. He just couldn't believe it. So after the session he offered to

get Charlie an 802 Union card, because Charlie didn't have an 802 card at that particular time. I don't know what else he offered him and whether Charlie ever took him up on it or not. I really don't know.
